properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 18 at 4:49PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from Craig Key to Halfmoon Shoal
out 20 nm...

At 449 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists detected a a
strong thunderstorm, capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots.
This thunderstorm was located 7 nm southwest of Sombrero Key Light,
moving west at 15 knots.

Locations that will be affected include...
Sombrero Key Light, Looe Key Light, and Big Pine Shoal.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for thunderstorms with wind gusts near 30 knots, locally
rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM OVER THE WATERS

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Yakutat; Glacier Bay; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 18 at 12:33PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river is expected to move into the NE Gulf Coast
Monday night and continue through Tuesday. Multiple periods of heavy
rain are expected for the Icy Strait corridor and northeast Gulf
Coast, including the following communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove,
Pelican, Gustavus, Juneau, Haines, and Skagway. Elevated gusty winds
are expected alongside this heavier rainfall, with the strongest
winds from the southwest expected late Tuesday morning into Tuesday
afternoon. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce
significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas
is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Eastern Gulf Coast, Northeast Gulf
Coast and Northern Inner Channels. This includes the cities of
Yakutat, Gustavus, Elfin Cove, And Pelican.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Isolated landslides are
possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Yakutat area between Monday morning and
Tuesday evening range between 4-6 inches, with greater than 8
inches possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. For Elfin
Cove, Pelican, and Gustavus, rain totals ranging between 2-4
inches, exceeding 6 inches on south to southwest facing mountains
along the outer coast, and exceeding 4 inches on south to
southwest facing mountains at elevation in Glacier Bay and around
Gustavus.

Coinciding with high rain rates, possibly exceeding 0.3 inches

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 18 at 12:33PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river is expected to move into the NE Gulf Coast
Monday night and continue through Tuesday. Multiple periods of heavy
rain are expected for the Icy Strait corridor and northeast Gulf
Coast, including the following communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove,
Pelican, Gustavus, Juneau, Haines, and Skagway. Elevated gusty winds
are expected alongside this heavier rainfall, with the strongest
winds from the southwest expected late Tuesday morning into Tuesday
afternoon. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will produce
significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas
is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Central Inner Channels and Northern
Inner Channels. This includes the city of Juneau.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Juneau area between Monday morning and
Tuesday evening range between 2-4 inches, with the highest totals
along south and southwest facing mountain slopes. For areas of
elevation greater than 1000 ft, rain totals may exceed 4 inches.
Highest rain rates are expected overnight Monday into Tuesday
with rain rates as high as 0.2 inches per hour.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Kent; Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 18 at 4:31PM EDT until October 20 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...From 3 PM to 9 PM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional elevated high tide cycles beyond
Tuesday evening are expected with additional coastal flood
hazards likely being needed.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 18 at 4:04PM EDT until October 18 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Onslow County beaches.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
properties.instruction:
Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM EDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 18 at 4:04PM EDT until October 22 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 3 feet of inundation
above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9
to 15 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves, and strong
longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 AM EDT Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from
shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a
swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and
back injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 18 at 4:04PM EDT until October 20 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation
above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 10 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves
expected, and strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday. For
the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. There is a possibility of being
stranded on Ocracoke for multiple days. This could be life
threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first
into the bottom causing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore
currents will create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This is a long duration event with
uncertainty on when conditions will improve. Significant ocean
overwash impacts are expected at vulnerable oceanside areas
through multiple high tide cycles into the work week. Minor
soundside water level rises will also be possible.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.
